entrypoints.summary: GET / accepts a string url query parameter and invokes page.goto(url) in headless Firefox.
The documented procedure uses first a visit that seeds IndexedDB and then a visit to the resulting profile file URI.

affected_components.role: Accepts attacker URL, launches Firefox with fixed userDataDir, and calls page.goto.

code_slices.surrounding_context: The official solution supplies the subsequent IndexedDB storage, profile file URI navigation, UTF-16 script inclusion, and beacon-decoding payload.
code_slices.vulnerable: The bot uses userDataDir: '/tmp/firefox-userdata' and navigates to the supplied URL with page.goto(url).

negative_controls: No bundled browser-run output demonstrates a failed control or hardened configuration.
observability.positive_marker: The official solution directs the operator to check the logger endpoint for the leaked flag; the bundled flag file provides expected secret data.

preconditions: The bot accepts attacker URLs and uses a fixed user-data directory.
Profile state from a first bot visit remains available to a second.
The IndexedDB backing-file URI is available or discoverable.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: IndexedDB Blob with Error prototype getter, UTF-16LE script inclusion, and beacon decoder.
trigger_steps.summary: Submit attacker content that creates an IndexedDB Blob containing file-origin exploit HTML.
Submit the generated profile backing file's file:// URI for bot navigation.

capabilities.concept: local-file contents encoded in a script error message

mitigations.concept: isolated browser profiles and denied untrusted file navigation

relation_candidates.rationale: The bot accepts a supplied URL and retains a fixed userDataDir; the documented first visit writes attacker HTML into IndexedDB in that profile.
The second documented visit targets the IndexedDB backing file below the reused profile, which is stated to be sniffed as HTML.

relation_candidates.dst: local-file contents encoded in a script error message
relation_candidates.rationale: The payload installs the error-name getter and includes file:///flag.txt using UTF-16LE charset.
The payload decodes error-derived UTF-16 code units and provides the result to navigator.sendBeacon.
relation_candidates.src: local-file contents encoded in a script error message

relation_candidates.rationale: The payload sends decoded data by beacon and the target is the supplied challenge flag file.

relation_candidates.dst: isolated browser profiles and denied untrusted file navigation
relation_candidates.rationale: This inferred hardening prevents later file:// execution of an attacker-created profile artifact; no patch establishes a specific implementation.

impact.attacker_capability: Cause the bot to beacon decoded contents derived from file:///flag.txt to an attacker-controlled endpoint.
impact.security_effect: Disclosure and exfiltration of a local secret file available to the browser process.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker supplies a URL to the bot endpoint, which launches Firefox using fixed /tmp/firefox-userdata and visits it.
Attacker web content persists an HTML Blob in IndexedDB, then a later visit targets its backing file beneath the reused Firefox profile; the solution says the file is sniffed as HTML.
The file-origin HTML installs a getter on ReferenceError.prototype.name, loads file:///flag.txt as a UTF-16LE script, and decodes the undefined-identifier error-message code units.
The payload sends decoded bytes to an attacker endpoint with navigator.sendBeacon, disclosing the challenge secret in /flag.txt.

failure.operation: File-origin execution of an IndexedDB backing artifact followed by UTF-16 script inclusion and interception of ReferenceError message construction.

primary_invariant.statement: Web-origin content stored in a browser profile must not become attacker-executable file-origin HTML that can include protected local files and expose parse/error-derived content.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The fixed profile is reused across attacker-directed visits; the official solution stores attacker HTML in IndexedDB and reopens its backing file through file://, which it states is sniffed as HTML before loading file:///flag.txt.

quality.review_notes: Official writeups and bot source document the intended chain and concrete payload, but no bundled end-to-end execution log or self-contained current harness proves a run. The concise procedure depends on historical external services and profile-dependent paths. No producer remediation patch is bundled; mitigations are design guidance. A separate unintended direct file-fetch route involving Puppeteer Firefox file-origin policy is explicitly excluded.

remediation.invariant_restored: Do not reuse attacker-writable browser-profile storage as a file:// navigation source; deny untrusted file-scheme navigation and retain strict separation between distinct local file origins.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Store attacker HTML in IndexedDB under the bot's reused Firefox profile, then obtain or brute-force its profile-dependent backing-file path.
data_structure_invariants: IndexedDB backing files from web content must not become privileged file-origin documents.
Local-file content must not be exposed through an attacker-observable script-error channel.
state_context.state_machine: First visit seeds an IndexedDB backing artifact in the fixed profile; subsequent visit targets that file:// path, where it is used as HTML and includes the flag file.

target.component: Express URL-submission endpoint and Puppeteer Firefox visitor with fixed user-data directory
